cells.value:
Require any of the Display Screen Equipment (DSE) to be able to bring up any of the pictures as well as normal personal computing interfaces

Requires 2-man operation

Due to fact that DCS is not reliable, operators are forced to monitor and operate off back wall

Too many actions required to carry out simple operation

Inability to handle large amounts of information

All visitors enter control room

Anyone seeking signature from Shift Supervisor also enters control room

- In some cases visitors 'hang around' when Shift Supervisor is not there and interact with on duty control room operators (CROs)

Integration of normal personal computer (PC) screen onto DCS

Information on control monitoring system (CMS) is fragmented and therefore difficult to interpret

Needs visual and auditable contact with CROs

Requires to be adjacent to PCF to sign off permits to work

Because Shift Supervisor sits in same room as CROs, confidential talks are carried out in any office that can be found (not ideal for good people management); this includes discussions with visitors

Lighting:

- Direct lighting creates glare on DSE and cannot be controlled by operators

- Lighting at Scheduler's office is poor and makeshift glare barriers have been erected.

- During night shift, back wall hard-wired outputs difficult to read

Thermal Environment

- Variable air conditioning and poor ventilation causes CROs to constantly take off and put on jackets during the course of a shift

- Complaints that the CCR is too warm in the summer and too cold in the winter

Noise

- Non-enclosed dot-matrix printers that provide data every 15 minutes are a distraction and add to overall background noise of the CCR

Mixture of controls that have been added as new systems are included in the project

Safeguard that protects against inadvertent operation also covers the label for the control (therefore stickers are used to identify controls that cannot be seen)

Automatic Shutdown (ASD) required to be on same panel (needs to be able to incorporate expansion)

Requires that all controls are within view of operator
Does not need visual contact with Shift Supervisor
